newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs set new closing high, many tempted to sell.
newsitem.headline: OLOs set new closing high, many tempted to sell.

text.p: Belgian linear bond futures closed at a new historical high of 119.84 on Wednesday, up 26, after touching an intraday high of 120.04, but dealers said the market was nervous and ready to take profit.
The 2006 benchmark yield ended at 6.04 percent, from 6.07, after hitting 6.01 in early trade. Its yield spread was an unchanged 13 bps over Bunds.
"The six percent level will be hard to break," said one Luxembourg-based dealer. He said his personal bet was that 10-year Belgian yields would stand around 6.35 percent at the end of December.

He added that he saw no reason why U.S. President Bill Clinton's election victory or Russian president Boris Yeltsin's succesful heart operation should boost bond prices. "In both cases, an existing situation has been confirmed," he said.
Another dealer said he saw no great danger of a sell-off before year-end and saw Bund futures moving to 101 and even 102. They stood 23 bp higher at 100.35 at 1645 GMT, after soaring to 100.47.
Belgium's yield premium over Germany was unaffected by news the European Commission, in its 1996/97 economic forecasts, had confirmed debt and deficit targets set in Belgium's 1997 budget.
The EU executive body sees Belgium's public sector deficit at 3.3 percent of GDP in 1996 and 2.9 percent in 1997. Belgium's debt/GDP ratio is seen at 130.6 in 1996 and 127.0 in 1997.
